title: The Secret Life of Red Foxes
body_text: The red fox (Vulpes vulpes) is the most widely distributed wild carnivore in the world. With its orange-red coat, pointed ears, and bushy white-tipped tail, this cunning and adaptable animal thrives everywhere from remote forests to city suburbs. Foxes are largely solitary hunters, relying on keen hearing to locate small prey like rodents hidden under snow or leaf litter.

title: Wolves of the Northern Forest
body_text: Gray wolves are highly social animals that live and hunt in tightly bonded packs. A wolf pack's territory can span hundreds of square miles as they track migrating elk and deer herds through dense boreal forest. Unlike the solitary fox, cooperation is the wolf's defining survival strategy.

title: Why Dogs Are Man's Best Friend
body_text: Domesticated over 15,000 years ago, dogs have become deeply woven into human life as companions, workers, and family members. Their loyalty, trainability, and emotional attunement to people set them apart from their wild canine relatives.

title: Brown Bears Before Hibernation
body_text: As autumn arrives, brown bears enter a feeding frenzy called hyperphagia, consuming up to 20,000 calories a day to build fat reserves. This massive, powerful animal will spend the coming winter in a den, its heart rate dropping dramatically as it sleeps through the cold months.

title: Deer in the Morning Mist
body_text: White-tailed deer are most active at dawn and dusk, grazing quietly at the edges of meadows and forests. Their large ears and keen sense of smell make them exceptionally alert to nearby predators, and a raised white tail is a classic alarm signal to the rest of the herd.

title: Mountain Lakes at Sunrise
body_text: There is nothing quite like watching the sun break over a still alpine lake, the water perfectly mirroring the surrounding peaks. This piece has no animal subject at all — it's here deliberately, as a case where 'no confident match' should be the correct system response if no landscape image exists in the corpus.
